skill.name: bmad-orchestrator
skill.description: Orchestrates BMAD workflows for structured AI-assisted development, from project setup through analysis, planning, solutioning, and implementation phase gates.
skill.summary: Routes BMAD projects through phased planning, status tracking, and review gates.
skill.author: supercent-io

security_audit.summary: The skill is a legitimate BMAD workflow orchestrator, and most static hits are markdown examples, /dev/null redirection, or fixed local parsing commands. The material risks are the remote pipe-to-shell plannotator installer, execution of a sibling hook script, and a Python fallback that interpolates user input into source code.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to sh.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl | sh with a pinned package install or a download-then-verify flow using checksums and clear user confirmation.

remediation.issue: Phase review fallback interpolates DOC_FILE and TITLE into Python source.
remediation.suggestion: Pass values to Python through argv or environment variables and call subprocess.run with a fixed argument list.

remediation.issue: Installer executes a sibling plannotator hook script without integrity checks.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit path, verify the dependency version, and ask for confirmation before running code from another skill.

remediation.issue: Review script can submit any readable local file path to plannotator.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict review inputs to configured BMAD output folders or require confirmation for paths outside the project docs directory.

semantic_findings.title: User-Controlled Python Code Injection in Review Fallback
semantic_findings.description: The phase review fallback builds a python3 -c program with DOC_FILE and TITLE interpolated into quoted Python source. A crafted filename or title containing quotes can alter the Python program if the fallback path runs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: DOC_FILE and TITLE are user-controlled arguments and are inserted directly into Python source before subprocess.run. The issue depends on the fallback path, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Installer Executes Sibling Skill Hook Without Provenance Check
semantic_findings.description: The installer resolves ../plannotator/scripts/setup-hook.sh and runs it when present. This executes code outside the audited skill boundary without verifying source, version, or integrity.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The path and bash execution are explicit in the installer. The intended integration is legitimate, but the absence of provenance checks makes the trust-boundary risk clear.

content.value_statement: Complex AI-assisted projects can lose track of phase status, required documents, and review gates. This skill adds BMAD workflow routing, initialization, status checks, and phase review guidance for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Initializes BMAD project folders and configuration files from templates.
Reads workflow status files and recommends the next BMAD phase command.
Routes projects through Analysis, Planning, Solutioning, and Implementation phases.
Validates BMAD YAML configuration fields with yq or basic shell parsing.
Submits phase documents to plannotator for review before phase transitions.
Documents Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, and OpenCode usage patterns.
limitations: Codex and OpenCode usage depends on an external orchestration bridge.
The installer can run external plannotator setup code and should be reviewed before use.
Status parsing is lightweight when yq is not installed.
The skill does not replace product judgment or human phase approval.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap a Structured Project
use_cases.description: Create BMAD folders, configuration, and workflow status files for a new software project.

use_cases.title: Control Phase Transitions
use_cases.description: Check required planning documents and route teams to the next valid BMAD phase.

use_cases.title: Review Deliverables Before Build
use_cases.description: Send PRDs, technical specs, and architecture documents through a review gate before implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize BMAD
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project
prompt_templates.prompt: Use bmad-orchestrator to initialize this project. Ask for any missing project name, type, level, and output folder before creating files.

prompt_templates.title: Check Workflow Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Use bmad-orchestrator to inspect the current BMAD status and tell me the next valid phase command with the reason.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Phase Gate
prompt_templates.prompt: Use bmad-orchestrator to prepare the current PRD or architecture document for phase gate review. Do not advance until approval is recorded.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Phase Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use bmad-orchestrator to audit this repository for BMAD readiness. Check config, status, required documents, phase rules, and review gate gaps.

output_examples.input: Check where this BMAD project is in the workflow.
output_examples.output: The project is in Planning. The PRD is required and not started. The next recommended command is /prd.

output_examples.input: Initialize BMAD for a level 2 web app named Atlas.
output_examples.output: BMAD configuration was prepared for Atlas with docs as the output folder. Planning and architecture phases are required for this level.

output_examples.input: Can we move from Planning to Solutioning?
output_examples.output: Not yet. The required planning document needs review approval before the workflow can advance to Solutioning.

best_practices: Review installer scripts before running any command that downloads or executes external content.
Keep bmad/config.yaml and docs/bmm-workflow-status.yaml committed or otherwise tracked for team visibility.
Run a phase gate review after each major deliverable and record approval before advancing.
anti_patterns: Do not skip phase gates because a document exists without approval.
Do not submit sensitive local files to plannotator as review documents.
Do not edit workflow status manually unless automated updates fail and the change is reviewed.

faq.question: What is BMAD Orchestrator for?
faq.answer: It coordinates a structured BMAD development workflow with setup, status tracking, phase routing, and review gates.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill documents Claude Code usage and can configure a plannotator review hook through its installer.

faq.question: Does it work with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes, but Codex usage is described as an orchestration integration rather than the default direct execution path.

faq.question: Does the skill run external commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes Bash scripts for setup, initialization, status checks, validation, and phase review.

faq.question: Is the plannotator installer safe to run automatically?
faq.answer: No. The installer uses a remote pipe-to-shell command, so users should inspect it or install plannotator manually.

faq.question: Can it manage all project decisions automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow structure and recommendations, but humans should approve documents and phase transitions.
